prompt:
Produce ONE complete hyper-realistic integrated illustrated Schemin' 26 Week 11 cinematic memo page. The output is a **finished typeset portrait page**, never a lone visual still, contact sheet, PDF-looking form or prompt illustration. Portrait art may have two to three filmically connected camera beats on this ONE page when necessary for combat continuity; do not create spreadsheet cells or lazy grid borders. Maintain 9:16 framing with a high-quality native page target of 1080x1920 px, plus phone reading at 390x693 px.
ISSUE MASTHEAD (printed exactly once): SCHEMIN’ ’26 • WEEK 11
MAIN HEADLINE: The Carter Listens
MATCHUP DECK (printed exactly once): His Majesty’s Blood at D0nkey K0ng
PUBLICATION BODY (PRINT EXACTLY, no deletions or added unsupported facts): Austin’s final blow carried through the clash. Four hooves scraped for grip; Wilson’s enormous armored body pitched over the intact parapet and vanished into the raging, storm-churned water. The carter stopped breathing. Even Austin stepped to the edge, his gold belt still fixed at his waist. Waves battered the pier. Then Wilson’s dark head broke the foam—coughing, alive. Only when the great centaur reached toward shore did Austin release the small jester’s cap. “My jester,” he said, almost without triumph. His Majesty’s Blood 168.20 · D0nkey K0ng 129.75.
STORY MOTION: The fall is unmistakable, then a beat of feared silence, then identifiable survivor; pride returns last.
PHYSICAL BEAT SEQUENCE:
F (dominant upper 65% impact frame): From cart-height 3/4 view: Wilson in physically continuous four-hoof pose pitches over the unbroken stone parapet; axe remains plausibly in hand or follows known trajectory. The camera sees the violent lake beneath and Austin's hooded silhouette above, not an invisible attacker. ACTING: Transfer from F10 skid; no bridge damage, no invented fast river gorge.
G (lower 35% quiet survival echo): Waterside/low lens gives the large gorilla head emerging alive among huge whitecaps, splashes and foam with arm reaching toward plausible bank; inset of carter's still hands and Austin's red-eyed hood watching from same parapet, clear cause/space relation. ACTING: Two-step reaction: witness fears the worst, relief once Wilson resurfaces. Small cap coda only after survival and not blocking his face.
CHARACTER CORRECTION ABSOLUTE: Austin Byars is THE BELT KEEPER: COMPLETELY HOODED FACE, TWO LUMINOUS RED EYES, segmented BLACK armor, circular GOLD chest medallion, gold title belt, crimson-black ragged cape, ornate sword. No face, no exposed brown hair, no generic swordsman. This is not a human-faced knight. He cannot have visible ordinary hair or brown human eyes. Reference approved Commissioner October 18 PNG and identity crops. Wilson Look is ONE single gorilla upper torso seamlessly fused to four-legged four-hoof horse/centaur body with red-and-gold Arsenal battle armor and heavy war axe; use current four-hoof Oct18 lineup, not older contradictory biped reference. The carter, horse and canvas wagon remain a grounded working observer at left approach. The SAME intact narrow stone bridge and working lantern as Week 10 physical p33; Mountain Lake is visible on BOTH sides. Rain-glazed center stone reset, working wagon at left approach, both piers readable. No wider invented bridge, no missing cart.
WEATHER: Intense local storm squall: directional crosswind, whipping crimson cape and wagon canopy, leaves, cold rain, large wind-agitated waves hitting piers, loud whitecaps/spray beneath intact span. Founder asks for Wilson to fall into a river of raging water. Atlas presently authorizes the named water body as Mountain Lake; depict *violent churning storm water below the bridge*, record literal directional river/rapid hydrology as an outstanding geography decision rather than silently asserting a new river.
CONTINUITY OUT: Wilson alive, injured only if separately sourced (do not infer), the cart can cross later; Austin retains championship belt; cap may appear only after Wilson surfaces; no World permanence inferred.
TYPE DESIGN: Atmospheric negative-space typography in the actual cinematic picture. Reading order masthead -> large headline -> matchup -> body -> scene -> coda, with scene-led layout, readable letterforms, not bottom paragraph pasted onto a completed image. Print score only where official result is included in v.print_copy. If image-generation text is unreliable, deterministic compositor overlays exact text, never truncated. No visible page number or F##/P##, no internal gate text and no dated old TheFFHub win probabilities.
REJECT IF: exposed-face Austin, non-centaur Wilson, unearned fall, multiple duplicated independent combatant bodies inside one beat, disconnected axe/sword geometry, floaty physical motion, static standoff, no real charging/combat, visible folio ID, missing dialogue/publication body, unreadable 390px narrative, wrong venue or invented directional river rapids.

PHOTOGRAPHIC REALISM HARD GATE (FOUNDERS NOVEMBER 24 REFERENCE): Study physically believable fine wet gravel, irregular rain puddles, small droplets on grass, authentic muted dusk and shallow depth of field, not glossy game CGI. Transfer only LIGHT/MATERIAL/LENS accuracy, NOT that road as the scene location. For this scene: Wetted armor with real spray and wave physics; thick whitecaps and real gravity at parapet, identifiable living head.. Low carter POV then spray-level survivor lens; lake not river. Work with subtle naturally motivated light, varying moisture, actual contact shadows, truthful material wear and physically accurate scene motion. Preserve exactly the original screenplay and typography. Master final text overlay at 4K, preserve correct faces/lips and dialogue. Do not alter the Founder-approved P09 candidate unless specifically instructed.

RENDER HARD VETO — ENDING SCORE BANNER: On the finished page P11 (internal ID only, DO NOT PRINT IT), visibly include final-result crimson/gold plaque with exact user-visible text 'His Majesty's Blood 168.20  •  D0nkey K0ng 129.75'. This is as required as the survival image and full manuscript. If missed, hold image for correction; do not regenerate or rewrite any story scene when repairing the banner. No internal folio labels.
